cells: Radioactive decay and residual heat melt rocks into magma.
Magma rises at convergent and divergent boundaries.
Water lowers melting point of mantle rocks.

blocks.content: Volcanism is driven by the upward movement of molten rock (magma) caused by density contrasts, pressure changes, and tectonic plate interactions.

items: Deccan Traps in India were formed by intraplate hotspot volcanism (Reunion Hotspot) during the Late Cretaceous period.
Mid-Ocean Ridge volcanism produces fluid basaltic magma with low silica content, whereas subduction zone volcanoes yield silica-rich, viscous andesitic/rhyolitic magma.
Questions frequently contrast explosive (convergent) versus effusive (divergent/hotspot) eruption styles.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Volcanism is primarily driven by the upward movement of magma due to lower density relative to surrounding mantle and crustal rocks.
Convergent boundaries lead to explosive volcanism via subduction and volatile-driven melting of mantle rock.
Divergent boundaries create effusive basaltic volcanism through decompression melting as tectonic plates pull apart.
Mantle plumes and hotspots generate intraplate volcanism independent of plate boundaries, such as the Hawaiian chain and Reunion hotspot.
The trapped gases (water vapor, CO2, SO2) under high pressure provide the expansive force for explosive volcanic eruptions.
